evidence.label: def:p15-occam-model - measurable input space, finite label set, nonempty finite or countable class of measurable functions fixed before the sample, fixed target in H, m>=1 independent observations with law P, ordered sample with repeats, consistency, generalization and empirical error, nonempty version space, proper consistent learner, roles of epsilon and delta, measurable selection, countable power-set setting for encoded claims. Held source opened: PDF p.2 (IPL 24 p.378) sec. 2 fixed domain and finite range, learning algorithm outputs a consistent member of H, independent observations under a fixed P with product law P^m, error definition, footnote 2; PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379) countable domain in the encoded setting.

thm:p15-occam-finite - strict bound r(1-eps)^m <= r e^{-m eps} for every consistent member, sample size with the -ln(1-eps) denominator and the eps-denominator replacement, uniformity in P and f, statistical-only remark. Held source PDF p.2 (IPL 24 p.378) Lemma 2.1 (strict 'less than (1-eps)^m r'), its proof by the events E_i^m and subadditivity, the restatement and the ln r + ln(1/delta) sample size; PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379) first line: it holds if m > (1/eps)(ln r + ln(1/delta)).

annex:p15.occam-finite - written proof: fixed-h agreement probability, independence, union over the fixed bad set, strict inequality, empty-set case, coverage of every consistent selection, q >= eps by the integral, (1-eps)^m <= e^{-m eps}, measurability, no use of a particular P or target.

thm:p15-occam-threshold-example - complete finite instance: class, target, tolerance, exact survival probability 2(2/3)^m-(1/3)^m, minimal m=10 with exact values at 9 and 10, generic bound 16, non-identifying 0/2 sample. Editorial example carrying no source attribution; it instantiates Lemma 2.1 of the held source (PDF p.2, IPL 24 p.378).

annex:p15.occam-threshold-example - written proof: hypothesis errors, survivor events and the containment of the h_0 event, inclusion-exclusion, monotone decrease, exact fractions with integer comparisons, ceiling 16 from 4^15 < 80*3^15 and 4^16 > 80*3^16, version space for the 0/2 sample.

def:p15-occam-codes - binary code set with a fixed decoding map onto H, several codes per function, length and minimum length l(h), empty code, conventions fixed before data, prefix-free definition with the empty-code boundary, countable X with effective encodings and polynomial-time testing of a represented hypothesis on an encoded observation. Held source PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379): complexity as the number of bits needed in a fixed encoding, countable domain, footnote 3 polynomial-time consistency check; Theorem 2.3 proof: hypotheses given by binary strings of bounded length.

thm:p15-occam-code-count - arbitrary-string count 2^{floor(L)+1}-1 < 2^{L+1}, prefix-free count 2^{floor(L)}, Kraft inequality, shortest-code Kraft sum, three-code boundary at length one. Held source PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379) Theorem 2.3 proof counts r <= 2^{n^c m^alpha} for strings of length at most n^c m^alpha (the entry separates the arbitrary-string and prefix-free conventions); PDF p.2 (IPL 24 p.378) Lemma 2.1 consumes the count r.

annex:p15.occam-code-count - written proof: geometric string count, hypotheses injected into codes at b=floor(L), disjoint depth-b descendant sets, finite-depth Kraft and the 2^b count, limit over all codes, shortest-code subfamily, three-string boundary.

def:p15-occam-algorithm - constants c>=1 and 0<=a<1, proper consistent learner, output code length at most n^c m^a for every n>=1, every f with l(f)<=n and every nonempty sample, runtime polynomial in encoded sample length, constants and representation independent of f,P,n,m,eps,delta; summary of the source's polynomial learnability; boundary that no existence claim is made. Held source PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379) Definition 2.2 (i)-(ii) and the polynomial-learnability definition (a)-(b) relative to a fixed encoding; PDF p.2 (IPL 24 p.378) definition of a learning algorithm (consistent output in H).

thm:p15-occam-compression - arbitrary-code sample bound with ln(2/delta), prefix-free replacement reproducing the source's displayed bound, O-bound with constants depending only on c,a, polynomial learnability conclusion. Held source PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379) Theorem 2.3 statement, displayed sufficient m >= max{2 ln(1/delta)/(-ln(1-eps)), (2 n^c ln2/(-ln(1-eps)))^{1/(1-alpha)}}, and its proof; PDF p.2 (IPL 24 p.378) Lemma 2.1 used in that proof.

annex:p15.occam-compression - written proof: sample-independent finite class H_L containing every output and the target, count < 2^{L+1}, algebra from the second lower bound, failure <= 2e^{-qm/2} <= delta, prefix-free variant, a=0, O-bound with absorption of ln2/eps, polynomiality in n,1/eps,1/delta, runtime premise.

thm:p15-occam-minimum-approximation - sample-independent output length n^c with explicit bounds for arbitrary and prefix-free codes; approximate minimizer of length at most b_+(S)^c; exact minimization sufficient but not required. Held source PDF p.4 (IPL 24 p.380) alpha=0 special case, sample size O((n^c+ln(1/delta))/eps) and meaning of the n^c term; PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379) NP-hard exact minimum-consistency and the weakened minimality criterion; PDF p.1 (IPL 24 p.377) abstract on nearly minimum consistent hypotheses.

annex:p15.occam-minimum-approximation - written proof: union bound over codes of length at most n^c, explicit delta bound, prefix-free replacement, b(S) <= n and b_+(S) <= n, approximate minimizer meets the a=0 Occam condition, exact minimizer as the c=1 case under the runtime premise.

thm:p15-occam-weighted - positive weights fixed before sampling with sum at most one, simultaneous bound over V(S) (hence for any selected consistent hypothesis), uninformative-bound boundary, prefix-free and arbitrary-code weights with their numerators, not a posterior. Editorial extension carrying no source attribution; held source PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379) complexity for a countably infinite class, PDF p.2 (IPL 24 p.378) Lemma 2.1 as the finite case.

annex:p15.occam-weighted - written proof: thresholds t_h, cases t_h >= 1 and 0 < t_h < 1, per-hypothesis bound delta*w_h, countable subadditivity, Kraft weights, arbitrary-code weight sum computed, no posterior normalization.

thm:p15-occam-boundaries - dependence case (1/2 against 2^{-m}), distribution-change case (training error zero, future error one), data-dependent two-member class with error >= 1-m/N (>= 1/2 when N >= 2m), fixed-representation premise, empty version space under conflicting labels. Editorial; held source PDF p.2 (IPL 24 p.378) independent observations under a fixed P and footnote 2 (errors in the sample ignored); PDF p.3 (IPL 24 p.379) fixed encoding.
annex:p15.occam-boundaries - written proofs of the three constructions and of the conflicting-label case.

thm:p15-occam-unseen-labels - lower bound (1/2)(1-m/N) for any learner with independent internal randomization, at least 1/4 when N >= 2m, explicitly labelled editorial. No source attribution; held source PDF p.3 and p.4 (IPL 24 pp. 379-380) sample sizes depend on the target complexity n.

annex:p15.occam-unseen-labels - written proof: uniform random target independent of data and learner, conditional fair-bit error at unobserved points, count of unobserved points, m > N case, averaging to a fixed target.

def:p15-occam-method - steps: specify population and target labels, fix class and encoding before sampling, state properness, consistency, output-size and runtime bounds, choose eps,delta and the sample size from the applicable theorem; conclusion scope and exclusions. No step requires independent sampling or a target-size bound n.
def:p15-occam-model - independence of X_1,...,X_m with common law P is a hypothesis of every guarantee the method invokes.
thm:p15-occam-boundaries item 1 - with dependent (repeated) observations the guarantee fails: probability 1/2 instead of 2^{-m}.
def:p15-occam-algorithm - the output-size bound n^c m^a is relative to a target-size bound n with l(f) <= n.
thm:p15-occam-compression - the sample size the method tells the user to choose depends on n.

components.gap: Hypotheses element not supplied in complete form; failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. The procedure (lines 251-255) never requires that the m training observations be independent draws with the population law P, the def:p15-occam-model hypothesis (lines 20-21) whose removal thm:p15-occam-boundaries item 1 (lines 213-216) shows defeats the guarantee, yet its conclusion (lines 257-258) asserts 'the stated probability over the sample'. It also never requires fixing a target-size bound n with l(f) <= n (target in the fixed represented class), on which the 'required output-size' bound n^c m^a (line 130) and the sample sizes of thm:p15-occam-compression (lines 147-151) and thm:p15-occam-minimum-approximation (lines 171-173) depend, so 'choose the sample size from the applicable theorem' cannot be executed from the stated steps. The method restates the learner-side premises and the fixed-before-sampling premise as explicit steps but omits these data-side premises; the sibling methods def:p15-conc-reference-method (handbook/parts/p15/bounded-concentration-learning.tex 444-445) and def:p15-w02b-p15-064-method (handbook/parts/p15/statistical-learning-and-generalization-w02b-p15-064.tex 362-363) do state the sampling/dependence assumption.

defect_observations.observation: def:p15-occam-codes: duplicated wording 'assume that testing ... is assumed to take polynomial time' (prose defect, not a coverage gap).

def:p15-occam-algorithm: the summary of the source's polynomial learnability omits the source's requirement that the algorithm be a learning algorithm for H (consistent output in H, IPL 24 p.378) and leaves clause (a)'s error-at-most-eps-with-probability-at-least-1-delta criterion implicit in 'sufficient'; the source's 'minimal sample size m(eps,delta,n)' (p.379) is rendered as 'sufficient'. Not counted against C006 because Definition 2.2 itself is reproduced completely and the Occam algorithm is defined as a proper consistent learner (line 127).

def:p15-occam-model attributes 'the full power-set sigma-field' to 'the source's encoded computational setting'; the held source (p.379) states only that X is countable. Editorial measure-theoretic gloss, not flagged as a failure.

thm:p15-occam-finite states the corollary 'with probability at least 1-delta'; the source (p.378) says 'larger than 1-delta'. The strict form follows from the strict display at lines 51-52 but is not stated.

thm:p15-occam-compression does not say in words that the source's own counting step r <= 2^{n^c m^alpha} for binary strings of length at most n^c m^alpha (p.379) undercounts arbitrary strings (2^{floor(L)+1}-1 by thm:p15-occam-code-count); the reader infers it from 'under that counting convention'.

thm:p15-occam-minimum-approximation, first paragraph: the guarantee (error at most eps with probability at least 1-delta) and the quantifier over targets of length at most n are left implicit by reference to thm:p15-occam-compression; the source's alpha=0 display O((n^c+ln(1/delta))/eps) (p.380) is not displayed, though it follows from lines 171-173 with q >= eps (annex lines 29-32) or from lines 157-161 at a=0.

annex:p15.occam-code-count: the disjointness argument names only codes of different lengths; equal-length distinct codes sharing an extension (impossible) is left implicit. Lines 106-108: the three-code boundary presumes the three codes decode to distinct hypotheses.

Section 171.4's title topic 'the distinction from minimum description length' is not drawn in occam-learning.tex; it is drawn here (sec:p15-rmdl-comparisons, thm:p15-rmdl-occam-case) and in handbook/parts/p15/statistical-learning-and-generalization-w02b-p15-064.tex lines 391-393. It lies outside the owed occam-learning components and was not assessed.
